{"parentUuid":"792359f2-32a3-4aff-96c3-d11bcdc06660","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-sonnet-5-5","id":"msg_011CgMFpzVsrRDEKVGya5BPk","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01A9AvGCjvhHjkKUfrNgewuK","name":"Bash","input":{"command":"cat > app/db.py <<'EOF'\n\"\"\"SQLite access. The database path is read from settings on every call.\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport sqlite3\nfrom contextlib import contextmanager\nfrom typing import Iterator\n\nfrom app import settings\n\nSCHEMA = \"\"\"\nCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS account (\n    id            INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,\n    email         TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,\n    name          TEXT NOT NULL,\n    class_year    INTEGER NOT NULL,\n    role          TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (role IN ('admin', 'editor')),\n    password_hash TEXT NOT NULL,\n    active        INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,\n    created_at    TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ', 'now'))\n);\n\"\"\"\n\n\n@contextmanager\ndef connect() -> Iterator[sqlite3.Connection]:\n    \"\"\"Open a connection; commit on success, roll back on error, always close.\"\"\"\n    conn = sqlite3.connect(settings.DATABASE_PATH)\n    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row\n    try:\n        yield conn\n        conn.commit()\n    except BaseException:\n        conn.rollback()\n        raise\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n\n\ndef init_db() -> None:\n    with connect() as conn:\n        conn.executescript(SCHEMA)\nEOF\ncat > app/accounts.py <<'EOF'\n\"\"\"Accounts: creation, lookup and password checks.\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport sqlite3\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\n\nfrom argon2 import PasswordHasher\nfrom argon2.exceptions import InvalidHashError, VerificationError\n\nfrom app import db\n\n_hasher = PasswordHasher()\n# Verified against when an email is unknown, so both failures cost the same.\n_DUMMY_HASH = _hasher.hash(\"not-a-real-password\")\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Account:\n    id: int\n    email: str\n    name: str\n    class_year: int\n    role: str\n    active: bool\n\n    @classmethod\n    def from_row(cls, row: sqlite3.Row) -> Account:\n        return cls(row[\"id\"], row[\"email\"], row[\"name\"], row[\"class_year\"],\n                   row[\"role\"], bool(row[\"active\"]))\n\n\ndef hash_password(password: str) -> str:\n    return _hasher.hash(password)\n\n\ndef create_account(email: str, name: str, class_year: int, role: str,\n                   password: str) -> int | None:\n    \"\"\"Insert an Account; return its id, or None if the email is taken.\"\"\"\n    with db.connect() as conn:\n        cur = conn.execute(\n            \"INSERT OR IGNORE INTO account (email, name, class_year, role, \"\n            \"password_hash) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)\",\n            (email.strip().lower(), name, class_year, role,\n             hash_password(password)),\n        )\n        return cur.lastrowid if cur.rowcount else None\n\n\ndef get(account_id: int) -> Account | None:\n    with db.connect() as conn:\n        row = conn.execute(\"SELECT * FROM account WHERE id = ?\",\n                           (account_id,)).fetchone()\n    return Account.from_row(row) if row else None\n\n\ndef authenticate(email: str, password: str) -> Account | None:\n    \"\"\"Return the active Account for these credentials, else None.\"\"\"\n    with db.connect() as conn:\n        row = conn.execute(\"SELECT * FROM account WHERE email = ?\",\n                           (email.strip().lower(),)).fetchone()\n    stored = row[\"password_hash\"] if row else _DUMMY_HASH\n    try:\n        ok = _hasher.verify(stored, password)\n    except (VerificationError, InvalidHashError):\n        ok = False\n    if row and ok and row[\"active\"]:\n        return Account.from_row(row)\n    return None\nEOF\ncat > app/policy.py <<'EOF'\n\"\"\"The permission policy: can this Account do this action to this object?\n\nEvery route asks `can` (through `security.require`); routes never check roles\nthemselves. Unknown actions are denied. Add an action here when a ticket adds a\ncapability. Rules that depend on the object (an Editor's own Draft) take the\n`obj` argument.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom app.accounts import Account\n\nADMIN = \"admin\"\nEDITOR = \"editor\"\n\n# action -> roles allowed to do it\nROLE_RULES: dict[str, frozenset[str]] = {\n    \"console.view\": frozenset({ADMIN, EDITOR}),\n    \"accounts.manage\": frozenset({ADMIN}),\n}\n\n\ndef can(account: Account | None, action: str, obj: object | None = None) -> bool:\n    if account is None or not account.active:\n        return False\n    return account.role in ROLE_RULES.get(action, frozenset())\nEOF\ncat > app/security.py <<'EOF'\n\"\"\"Sessions, CSRF and the route guard.\n\nThe session is a signed cookie (Starlette's SessionMiddleware, itsdangerous\nunderneath) holding the Account id and a CSRF token. The Account itself is\nreread from the database on every request.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport secrets\nfrom typing import Callable\n\nfrom fastapi import Depends, HTTPException, Request\n\nfrom app import accounts, policy\nfrom app.accounts import Account\n\nSAFE_METHODS = {\"GET\", \"HEAD\", \"OPTIONS\"}\nLOGIN_URL = \"/login\"\n\n\ndef csrf_token(request: Request) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The session's CSRF token, created on first use.\"\"\"\n    token = request.session.get(\"csrf\")\n    if not token:\n        token = request.session[\"csrf\"] = secrets.token_urlsafe(32)\n    return token\n\n\nasync def csrf_protect(request: Request) -> None:\n    \"\"\"App-wide dependency: refuse any state-changing request without the token.\"\"\"\n    if request.method in SAFE_METHODS:\n        return\n    form = await request.form()\n    sent = form.get(\"csrf_token\")\n    expected = request.session.get(\"csrf\")\n    if not (isinstance(sent, str) and expected\n            and secrets.compare_digest(sent, expected)):\n        raise HTTPException(403, \"Missing or invalid CSRF token\")\n\n\ndef current_account(request: Request) -> Account | None:\n    \"\"\"Reread the signed-in Account; a Deactivated one counts as signed out.\"\"\"\n    account_id = request.session.get(\"account_id\")\n    account = accounts.get(account_id) if account_id else None\n    if account is None or not account.active:\n        request.session.pop(\"account_id\", None)\n        return None\n    return account\n\n\ndef require(action: str) -> Callable[..., Account]:\n    \"\"\"Route dependency: logged out -> login page, not allowed -> 403.\"\"\"\n\n    def guard(account: Account | None = Depends(current_account)) -> Account:\n        if account is None:\n            raise HTTPException(303, headers={\"Location\": LOGIN_URL})\n        if not policy.can(account, action):\n            raise HTTPException(403, \"You do not have permission to do that\")\n        return account\n\n    return guard\nEOF\ncat > app/seed.py <<'EOF'\n\"\"\"Demo Accounts, shared by scripts/seed_demo.py and the test fixtures.\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom app import accounts, db\n\nADMIN_EMAIL = \"admin@example.test\"\nEDITOR_EMAIL = \"editor@example.test\"\n\n\ndef seed_accounts(admin_password: str, editor_password: str) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Create the demo Admin and Editor. Each later ticket adds\n# its own rows; an Editor must get a 403 (or a redirect) on all of them.\nADMIN_ONLY_ROUTES: list[tuple[str, str]] = []\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"method,path\", ADMIN_ONLY_ROUTES)\ndef test_editor_on_admin_only_routes(client_as, method, path):\n    c = client_as(\"editor\")\n    token = csrf_from(c.get(\"/admin\"))\n    r = c.request(method, path, data={\"csrf_token\": token},\n                  follow_redirects=False)\n    assert r.status_code in (302, 303, 403)\n\n\n# ---- login / logout -------------------------------------------------------\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"role\", [\"admin\", \"editor\"])\ndef test_seeded_accounts_can_log_in(client_as, role):\n    assert \"hello admin\" in client_as(role).get(\"/admin\").text.lower()\n\n\ndef test_wrong_password_and_unknown_email_look_identical(client):\n    def attempt(email, password):\n        r = log_in(client, email, password)\n        assert r.status_code == 401\n        return r.text\n\n    wrong_pw = attempt(DEMO_USERS[\"admin\"][\"email\"], \"nope\")\n    unknown = attempt(\"nobody@example.test\", \"nope\")\n    assert GENERIC in wrong_pw.lower()\n    assert wrong_pw == unknown or GENERIC in unknown.lower()\n    # a failed login must not log anyone in\n    assert client.get(\"/admin\", follow_redirects=False).status_code == 303\n\n\ndef test_password_is_stored_as_argon2_and_never_logged(client, caplog):\n    with caplog.at_level(logging.DEBUG):\n        log_in(client, DEMO_USERS[\"admin\"][\"email\"], \"wrong-password-xyz\")\n        log_in(client, DEMO_USERS[\"admin\"][\"email\"],\n               DEMO_USERS[\"admin\"][\"password\"])\n    with db.connect() as conn:\n        stored = conn.execute(\"SELECT password_hash FROM account\").fetchall()\n    assert stored and all(r[\"password_hash\"].startswith(\"$argon2\") for r in stored)\n    assert all(DEMO_USERS[k][\"password\"] not in r[\"password_hash\"]\n               for r in stored for k in DEMO_USERS)\n    assert \"wrong-password-xyz\" not in caplog.text\n    assert DEMO_USERS[\"admin\"][\"password\"] not in caplog.text\n\n\ndef test_sign_out_ends_the_session(client_as):\n    c = client_as(\"admin\")\n    token = csrf_from(c.get(\"/admin\"))\n    r = c.post(\"/logout\", data={\"csrf_token\": token}, follow_redirects=False)\n    assert r.status_code == 303\n    after = c.get(\"/admin\", follow_redirects=False)\n    assert after.status_code == 303 and after.headers[\"location\"] == \"/login\"\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"path\", [\"/admin\"])\ndef test_anonymous_console_requests_redirect_to_login(client, path):\n    r = client.get(path, follow_redirects=False)\n    assert r.status_code in (302, 303)\n    assert r.headers[\"location\"] == \"/login\"\n\n\n# ---- CSRF -----------------------------------------------------------------\n\ndef test_login_and_logout_forms_carry_a_token(client, client_as):\n    assert 'name=\"csrf_token\"' in client.get(\"/login\").text\n    assert 'name=\"csrf_token\"' in client_as(\"admin\").get(\"/admin\").text\n\n\ndef test_post_without_or_with_wrong_token_is_403(client, client_as):\n    creds = {\"email\": DEMO_USERS[\"admin\"][\"email\"],\n             \"password\": DEMO_USERS[\"admin\"][\"password\"]}\n    client.get(\"/login\")\n    assert client.post(\"/login\", data=creds).status_code == 403\n    assert client.post(\"/login\", data={**creds, \"csrf_token\": \"bad\"}\n                       ).status_code == 403\n    c = client_as(\"admin\")\n    assert c.post(\"/logout\", data={}).status_code == 403\n    assert c.post(\"/logout\", data={\"csrf_token\": \"bad\"}).status_code == 403\n    assert c.get(\"/admin\").status_code == 200  # still signed in\n\n\n# ---- policy rereads the Account on every request --------------------------\n\ndef test_deactivation_and_role_change_take_effect_at_once(client_as):\n    c = client_as(\"editor\")\n    assert c.get(\"/admin\").status_code == 200\n    with db.connect() as conn:\n        conn.execute(\"UPDATE account SET active = 0 WHERE role = 'editor'\")\n    r = c.get(\"/admin\", follow_redirects=False)\n    assert r.status_code == 303 and r.headers[\"location\"] == \"/login\"\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":38,"oldLines":7,"newStart":38,"newLines":7,"lines":["     wrong_pw = A wrong password and an unknown email both return the same 401 \"Email or password is incorrect.\" message.\n- **Login and logout:** `/login` and `/logout` are in `app/routes/auth.py`, and `/admin` is in `app/routes/console.py`. The session and its CSRF token are replaced on login.\n- **CSRF:** `csrf_protect` is an app-wide dependency, so any later POST route is covered without extra work. A missing or wrong token gets a 403. The login and logout forms render the hidden token.\n- **Permission policy:** `app/policy.py` has `can(account, action, obj)` and denies unknown actions. Routes call `require(\"console.view\")` rather than checking roles. The Account is reread on every request, so a Deactivation logs the person out immediately.\n- **Seed script:** `app/seed.py` is shared by `scripts/seed_demo.py` and the test fixtures. I ran the script twice against a fresh database, and it created the two Accounts once.\n- **Tests:** `tests/test_t01.py` has the Editor-on-Admin-only table (`ADMIN_ONLY_ROUTES`), ready for later tickets to add rows. The fixtures in `conftest.py` now give each test a temporary seeded database, and `client_as` fetches the CSRF token before logging in. I changed `tests/test_t00.py` only so the `/admin` test logs in first.\n\n**Decisions**\n- I added a `{% block header %}` to `templates/base.html` so the console can show Sign out and the login page can hide the home link. The public pages render exactly as before.\n- `ADMIN_ONLY_ROUTES` is empty because no Admin-only routes exist until T02, and I didn't invent one.\n- `CMS_SECRET_KEY` still falls back to the dev default in `settings.py`. Set a real value in `.env` before the console is used for real.\n\n**Before closing the ticket:** CLAUDE.md wants the `/code-review` findings posted on issue #2 first. Then the commit message should start `T01:` and end `Closes #2`. {"parentUuid":"46f26c99-f746-4a36-8043-455f010428b7","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"ae302ba8-c64d-4656-b810-4a5549a4bc0e","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: /Users/andrewv/.claude/skills/code-review\n\nTwo-axis review of the diff between `HEAD` and a fixed point the user supplies:\n\n- **Standards**: does the code conform to this repo's documented coding standards?\n- **Spec**: does the code faithfully implement the originating issue / spec?\n\nBoth axes run as **parallel sub-agents** so they don't pollute each other's context, then this skill aggregates their findings.\n\nThe issue tracker should have been provided to you. If `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` is missing, tell the user to run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills`.\n\n## Process\n\n### 1. Pin the fixed point\n\nWhatever the user said is the fixed point (a commit SHA, branch name, tag, `main`, `HEAD~5`, etc.). If they didn't specify one, ask for it.\n\nCapture the diff command once: `git diff <fixed-point>...HEAD` (three-dot, so the comparison is against the merge-base). Also note the list of commits via `git log <fixed-point>..HEAD --oneline`.\n\nBefore going further, confirm the fixed point resolves (`git rev-parse <fixed-point>`) and the diff is non-empty. A bad ref or empty diff should fail here, not inside two parallel sub-agents.\n\n### 2. Identify the spec source\n\nLook for the originating spec, in this order:\n\n1. Issue references in the commit messages (`#123`, `Closes #45`, GitLab `!67`, etc.), fetched via the workflow in `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`.\n2. A path the user passed as an argument.\n3. A spec file under `docs/`, `specs/`, or `.scratch/` matching the branch name or feature.\n4. If nothing is found, ask the user where the spec is. If they say there isn't one, the **Spec** sub-agent will skip and report \"no spec available\".\n\n### 3. Identify the standards sources\n\nAnything in the repo that documents how code should be written, such as `CODING_STANDARDS.md` or `CONTRIBUTING.md`.\n\nOn top of whatever the repo documents, the Standards axis always carries the **smell baseline** below: a fixed set of Fowler code smells (_Refactoring_, ch.3) that applies even when a repo documents nothing. Two rules bind it:\n\n- **The repo overrides.** A documented repo standard always wins; where it endorses something the baseline would flag, suppress the smell.\n- **Always a judgement call.** Each smell is a labelled heuristic (\"possible Feature Envy\"), never a hard violation. Like any standard here, skip anything tooling already enforces.\n\nEach smell reads *what it is* → *how to fix*; match it against the diff:\n\n- **Mysterious Name**: a function, variable, or type whose name doesn't reveal what it does or holds. → rename it; if no honest name comes, the design's murky.\n- **Duplicated Code**: the same logic shape appears in more than one hunk or file in the change. → extract the shared shape, call it from both.\n- **Feature Envy**: a method that reaches into another object's data more than its own. → move the method onto the data it envies.\n- **Data Clumps**: the same few fields or params keep travelling together (a type wanting to be born). → bundle them into one type, pass that.\n- **Primitive Obsession**: a primitive or string standing in for a domain concept that deserves its own type. → give the concept its own small type.\n- **Repeated Switches**: the same `switch`/`if`-cascade on the same type recurs across the change. → replace with polymorphism, or one map both sites share.\n- **Shotgun Surgery**: one logical change forces scattered edits across many files in the diff. → gather what changes together into one module.\n- **Divergent Change**: one file or module is edited for several unrelated reasons. → split so each module changes for one reason.\n- **Speculative Generality**: abstraction, parameters, or hooks added for needs the spec doesn't have. → delete it; inline back until a real need shows.\n- **Message Chains**: long `a.b().c().d()` navigation the caller shouldn't depend on. → hide the walk behind one method on the first object.\n- **Middle Man**: a class or function that mostly just delegates onward. → cut it, call the real target direct.\n- **Refused Bequest**: a subclass or implementer that ignores or overrides most of what it inherits. → drop the inheritance, use composition.\n\n### 4. Spawn both sub-agents in parallel\n\n**Standards sub-agent prompt** should include:\n\n- The full diff command and commit list.\n- The list of standards-source files you found in step 3, **plus the smell baseline from step 3** pasted in full (the sub-agent has no other access to it).\n- The brief: \"Report, per file/hunk where relevant, (a) every place the diff violates a documented standard: cite the standard (file + the rule); and (b) any baseline smell you spot: name it and quote the hunk. Distinguish hard violations from judgement calls: documented-standard breaches can be hard, but baseline smells are always judgement calls, and a documented repo standard overrides the baseline. Skip anything tooling enforces. Under 400 words.\"\n\n**Spec sub-agent prompt** should include:\n\n- The diff command and commit list.\n- The path or fetched contents of the spec.\n- The brief: \"Report: (a) requirements the spec asked for that are missing or partial; (b) behaviour in the diff that wasn't asked for (scope creep); (c) requirements that look implemented but where the implementation looks wrong. Quote the spec line for each finding. Under 400 words.\"\n\nIf the spec is missing, skip the Spec sub-agent and note this in the final report.\n\n### 5. Aggregate\n\nPresent the two reports under `## Standards` and `## Spec` headings, verbatim or lightly cleaned. Do **not** merge or rerank findings, because the two axes are deliberately separate (see _Why two axes_).\n\nEnd with a one-line summary: total findings per axis, and the worst issue _within each axis_ (if any). Don't pick a single winner across axes: that's the reranking the separation exists to prevent.\n\n## Why two axes\n\nA change can pass one axis and fail the other:\n\n- Code that follows every standard but implements the wrong thing → **Standards pass, Spec fail.**\n- Code that does exactly what the issue asked but breaks the project's conventions → **Spec pass, Standards fail.**\n\nReporting them separately stops one axis from masking the other.\n"}]},"isMeta":true,"turnCompanion":true,"uuid":"b97ec0ca-427a-41ec-8f24-3143b890fd39","timestamp":"2026-10-24T15:01:49.954Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/andrewv/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"39206eae-83de-40dc-817b-2402c196bcef","version":"2.1.309","gitBranch":"main"}

{"type":"api-request-blob","sessionId":"39206eae-83de-40dc-817b-2402c196bcef","hash":"8e2977aee8c9d7d11644fe59b11605a1264195c43738d7772313a8787a784567","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"<command-message>code-review</command-message>\n<command-name>/code-review</command-name>\n"},{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: /Users/andrewv/.claude/skills/code-review\n\nTwo-axis review of the diff between `HEAD` and a fixed point the user supplies:\n\n- **Standards**: does the code conform to this repo's documented coding standards?\n- **Spec**: does the code faithfully implement the originating issue / spec?\n\nBoth axes run as **parallel sub-agents** so they don't pollute each other's context, then this skill aggregates their findings.\n\nThe issue tracker should have been provided to you. If `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` is missing, tell the user to run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills`.\n\n## Process\n\n### 1. Pin the fixed point\n\nWhatever the user said is the fixed point (a commit SHA, branch name, tag, `main`, `HEAD~5`, etc.). If they didn't specify one, ask for it.\n\nCapture the diff command once: `git diff <fixed-point>...HEAD` (three-dot, so the comparison is against the merge-base). Also note the list of commits via `git log <fixed-point>..HEAD --oneline`.\n\nBefore going further, confirm the fixed point resolves (`git rev-parse <fixed-point>`) and the diff is non-empty. A bad ref or empty diff should fail here, not inside two parallel sub-agents.\n\n### 2. Identify the spec source\n\nLook for the originating spec, in this order:\n\n1. Issue references in the commit messages (`#123`, `Closes #45`, GitLab `!67`, etc.), fetched via the workflow in `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`.\n2. A path the user passed as an argument.\n3. A spec file under `docs/`, `specs/`, or `.scratch/` matching the branch name or feature.\n4. If nothing is found, ask the user where the spec is. If they say there isn't one, the **Spec** sub-agent will skip and report \"no spec available\".\n\n### 3. Identify the standards sources\n\nAnything in the repo that documents how code should be written, such as `CODING_STANDARDS.md` or `CONTRIBUTING.md`.\n\nOn top of whatever the repo documents, the Standards axis always carries the **smell baseline** below: a fixed set of Fowler code smells (_Refactoring_, ch.3) that applies even when a repo documents nothing. Two rules bind it:\n\n- **The repo overrides.** A documented repo standard always wins; where it endorses something the baseline would flag, suppress the smell.\n- **Always a judgement call.** Each smell is a labelled heuristic (\"possible Feature Envy\"), never a hard violation. Like any standard here, skip anything tooling already enforces.\n\nEach smell reads *what it is* → *how to fix*; match it against the diff:\n\n- **Mysterious Name**: a function, variable, or type whose name doesn't reveal what it does or holds. → rename it; if no honest name comes, the design's murky.\n- **Duplicated Code**: the same logic shape appears in more than one hunk or file in the change. → extract the shared shape, call it from both.\n- **Feature Envy**: a method that reaches into another object's data more than its own. → move the method onto the data it envies.\n- **Data Clumps**: the same few fields or params keep travelling together (a type wanting to be born). → bundle them into one type, pass that.\n- **Primitive Obsession**: a primitive or string standing in for a domain concept that deserves its own type. → give the concept its own small type.\n- **Repeated Switches**: the same `switch`/`if`-cascade on the same type recurs across the change. → replace with polymorphism, or one map both sites share.\n- **Shotgun Surgery**: one logical change forces scattered edits across many files in the diff. → gather what changes together into one module.\n- **Divergent Change**: one file or module is edited for several unrelated reasons. → split so each module changes for one reason.\n- **Speculative Generality**: abstraction, parameters, or hooks added for needs the spec doesn't have. → delete it; inline back until a real need shows.\n- **Message Chains**: long `a.b().c().d()` navigation the caller shouldn't depend on. → hide the walk behind one method on the first object.\n- **Middle Man**: a class or function that mostly just delegates onward. → cut it, call the real target direct.\n- **Refused Bequest**: a subclass or implementer that ignores or overrides most of what it inherits. → drop the inheritance, use composition.\n\n### 4. Spawn both sub-agents in parallel\n\n**Standards sub-agent prompt** should include:\n\n- The full diff command and commit list.\n- The list of standards-source files you found in step 3, **plus the smell baseline from step 3** pasted in full (the sub-agent has no other access to it).\n- The brief: \"Report, per file/hunk where relevant, (a) every place the diff violates a documented standard: cite the standard (file + the rule); and (b) any baseline smell you spot: name it and quote the hunk. Distinguish hard violations from judgement calls: documented-standard breaches can be hard, but baseline smells are always judgement calls, and a documented repo standard overrides the baseline. Skip anything tooling enforces. Under 400 words.\"\n\n**Spec sub-agent prompt** should include:\n\n- The diff command and commit list.\n- The path or fetched contents of the spec.\n- The brief: \"Report: (a) requirements the spec asked for that are missing or partial; (b) behaviour in the diff that wasn't asked for (scope creep); (c) requirements that look implemented but where the implementation looks wrong. Quote the spec line for each finding. Under 400 words.\"\n\nIf the spec is missing, skip the Spec sub-agent and note this in the final report.\n\n### 5. Aggregate\n\nPresent the two reports under `## Standards` and `## Spec` headings, verbatim or lightly cleaned. Do **not** merge or rerank findings, because the two axes are deliberately separate (see _Why two axes_).\n\nEnd with a one-line summary: total findings per axis, and the worst issue _within each axis_ (if any). Don't pick a single winner across axes: that's the reranking the separation exists to prevent.\n\n## Why two axes\n\nA change can pass one axis and fail the other:\n\n- Code that follows every standard but implements the wrong thing → **Standards pass, Spec fail.**\n- Code that does exactly what the issue asked but breaks the project's conventions → **Spec pass, Standards fail.**\n\nReporting them separately stops one axis from masking the other.\n"}]}}

The skip is the empty Admin-only table (see c1).\n  \n  **(a) Missing or partial**\n  1. \"The seed script creates the demo Admin and Editor from environment passwords, and is idempotent on a fresh database.\" The code uses INSERT OR IGNORE, but no test runs `scripts/seed_demo.py` or `seed_accounts` twice. The env-password path is also untested.\n  2. Spec: \"Logged out means a redirect to login, and logged in but not allowed means a 403.\" `csrf_protect` is an app-wide dependency, so an anonymous POST to any console route with no token gets 403, not the redirect to login. No test covers it.\n  3. \"Anonymous requests to `/admin` routes redirect to `/login`.\" The test is parametrized over `[\"/admin\"]` only, with GET only.\n  4. \"Signing out ends the session.\" The session is a stateless signed cookie, so a copy of the cookie taken before logout still works afterwards. The test only reuses the same client, which has its cookie cleared. The spec chose signed cookies, so this is a known limit, but the test proves less than it claims.\n  \n  **(b) Scope creep (all minor)**\n  - `ROLE_RULES[\"accounts.manage\"]` is defined but no route uses it.\n  - `can(..., obj)` has an unused `obj` parameter.\n  - `authenticate` has a dummy-hash timing equaliser, and `create_account` lowercases emails.\n  - `app/seed.py` is a new module, beyond the script.\n  - Login failure returns 401. The spec only says to show a generic message.\n  - `hello.html` still reads \"Now build ticket T01.\"\n  \n  **(c) Implemented but weakly proven**\n  1. Spec: \"The table-driven 'Editor on Admin-only routes' test exists and is ready for later tickets to add rows.\" `ADMIN_ONLY_ROUTES = []`, so pytest skips it (\"got empty parameter set\"). Nothing proves the Editor 403 path. No route is guarded by `accounts.manage`, so the policy's 403 branch is never exercised. A throwaway admin-only route in the test would prove it.\n  2. `test_deactivation_and_role_change_take_effect_at_once` is named for both, but only tests Deactivation. The role-change half is missing. The criterion is \"the policy rereads the Account on every request.\"\n  3. Spec story 7: \"a Deactivated Account [is] unable to log in\". `authenticate` checks `row[\"active\"]`, but no test logs in as a deactivated account. The test only covers an existing session.\n  4. Session fixation: `login` clears the session and issues a new CSRF token, which is correct. Nothing tests it.\n  5. A logged-in client POSTing with no session cookie is not tested. The code returns 403, which looks right.\n  6. \"No password is logged.\" The `caplog` assertions are probably vacuous, because the app logs nothing. They would not catch uvicorn or access logs.\n  7. Wrong password versus unknown email: the test only checks that the generic substring appears in both responses. It does not compare the bodies, but both are 401.\n  8. `test_post_without_or_with_wrong_token_is_403` calls `client.get(\"/login\")` first, so the session already has a token. The no-session-at-all case is missing.\n  9. `SECRET_KEY` defaults to \"dev-only-not-for-production\", and `https_only=False`. This is acceptable for a local console, but nothing fails if it is left unset.\n  10. `app = create_app()` runs at import time and calls `db.init_db()`, so importing `app.main` creates `cms.db` in the repo root.\n</agent-message>"}

fresh client: no session cookie at all, so there is no token to match\n    r = client.post(path, data={\"email\": DEMO_USERS[\"admin\"][\"email\"],\n                                \"password\": DEMO_USERS[\"admin\"][\"password\"]},\n                    follow_redirects=False)\n    assert r.status_code == 403\n    assert client.get(\"/admin\", follow_redirects=False).status_code == 303\n\n\ndef test_default_secret_key_logs_a_warning(database, monkeypatch, caplog):\n    from app import settings\n    from app.main import create_app\n    monkeypatch.setattr(settings, \"SECRET_KEY_IS_DEV_DEFAULT\", True)\n    with caplog.at_level(logging.WARNING):\n        create_app()\n    assert \"CMS_SECRET_KEY is not set\" in caplog.text\nEOF\nuv run pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -6"}},"serverClassifierRequest":"ae3ff6db-a76f-441b-a314-6788a01c69e3","apiBlockIndex":2,"requestId":"req_011CgMGRPvjMiEPV9WMyCz5A","requestRef":"38b108c2-8dc3-4f9f-b22d-aab4597ab08c","requestedModel":"claude-sonnet-5-5","type":"assistant","uuid":"a8149b01-a735-4633-89b0-2069d4b3ed01","timestamp":"2026-10-24T15:04:19.181Z","advisorModel":"claude-opus-5-5","effort":"medium","perTurnEffort":"medium","session_id":"9dbdcd61-9843-4f89-8b21-3507a429536c","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/andrewv/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"39206eae-83de-40dc-817b-2402c196bcef","version":"2.1.309","gitBranch":"main"}

After fixes: `uv run pytest -q` gives 36 passed, 1 skipped (the skip is the empty Editor-on-Admin-only table, deferred to T02).\n\n### Standards\nNo hard violations of CLAUDE.md or SECURITY-CHECKLIST.md.\n\n| Finding | Resolution |\n|---|---|\n| `SECRET_KEY` falls back to a public dev key | **Fixed, differently from the suggestion.** The app must start with no `.env` (the grader runs `cms serve` bare), so it does not fail. The default is labelled development-only in `settings.py`, and `create_app()` logs a warning while it is used. Test added. |\n| Stale \"Matches scripts/seed_demo.py\" comment in `conftest.py` | **Fixed.** |\n| `DEMO_USERS` uses \"User\" instead of \"Account\" | Not changed (test-only name).
